Fixes, following fix_plan_run-8800:
- D1, schedule shape: the evaluator reads explain_schedule tasks only from inputs.tasks. The test fixtures now mirror the real capture: schedule tasks, own_runs and open_escalations sit under inputs, and get_plan of the paused part carries no progress. A top-level legacy task list is rejected. A new CLI regression runs the unmodified qa-evidence/{plan,schedule,timeline,runs}.json with its manifest. In both modes it exits 1 with input_errors=[], completeness verified, and reasons plan_progress_missing, hold_after_plan, held_by_predecessor, progress_waiting, release_decision_missing and swe_run_missing. Missing progress still blocks a release.
- D2, inherited status keys: RUN_OUTCOME is now a Map over exactly pending→submitted, running→running, succeeded→finished and failed→finished. scheduled, cancelled and superseded are named as ignored. Any other value, including constructor, toString, __proto__ and hasOwnProperty, is reported as ignored with status_unsupported, keeps the raw status, and gives reason swe_run_status_unsupported. Covered by evaluator and CLI tests (exit 1, no dispatch_runs).
- D3, release recognition: the keyword blacklist is gone. Only a decision of kind after_plan_released with its own id counts, and its evidence must carry plan_id equal to the part exactly, predecessor_id, predecessor_status=abandoned and a non-empty parent_note. This is the receipt shape from plan.md playbook step 3. When --abandon-decision ids are supplied, abandon_decision_id and note_decision_id are compared to them by exact identity (a test shows dec-558050 is rejected), and at least one must be present. Prose is never read, and a shared trace does not authenticate a receipt. Each gap has a stable reason: release_plan_id_missing/mismatch, release_predecessor_missing/mismatch, release_predecessor_not_abandoned, release_note_missing, abandon_decision_ref_missing/mismatch, release_decision_id_missing, release_evidence_missing, release_decision_missing. QA's two D3 cases are regressions in both the evaluator and the CLI. A future mono-v2 receipt in another shape fails until the probe is taught that shape; I did not guess its schema.
- D4, missing run id: a matching SWE run without a non-empty id is reported as ignored run_id_missing with run_id null and reason swe_run_id_missing. "?" is never substituted. A second identified failed run still proves dispatch under its own id, and delivery_proven stays false.
- D5, completeness: the CLI exits 0 only when --manifest verifies all four snapshots. Without a manifest it reports a diagnosis, adds completeness_verified to unmet and exits 1. The evaluator rejects payloads that declare themselves partial (complete not true, has_more not false, truncated not false, or a non-empty next_cursor) as exit 2, with or without a manifest. get_timeline's own cursor does not count as a partial marker, and no list_runs pagination was introduced. The walkthrough documents all of this.

evidence.note: Abandon pm-248 as a plan, not as an accept. Seasons and the torn-sheet 404 were verified live at 1366x768 and 390x844 (probe-seasons 28/28, probe-lost 34/34), and the code for Ask the Ink's model tier is on main (npm test 1909 pass at 303eaa3, fake-model probe 53/53). The only failing outcome is production reach: GET/POST /api/ask are 404 and 0 of 17 deployed chunks carry api/ask. The causes are a stale Vercel deploy (esc-384) and ASK_LLM plus ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset (esc-383). Both need the account owner, and they are cost and external-account decisions. A replan would add no code, because the product owner cannot set a key or redeploy. It would also duplicate pm-255, which already holds the remaining Ask work: t-1557 deploy-bundle probe and t-1558 tier probe, queued after_plan pm-248. Abandoning frees pm-255 to run. This is not an accept: the Ask production outcome stays unmet until a person sets the env, redeploys, and a later acceptance sees GET /api/ask return 200 with enabled:true. The plan can be reopened with plan_manager_reopen_plan.
